entities.summary:
Bartholomew of Neocastro was an Italian jurist and author of a chronicle called the Historia Sicula, which covers the years from 1250 to 1293. This 14th-century work provides valuable insights into the politics, culture, and society of Sicily during the late Middle Ages. The Historia Sicula is notable for its detailed descriptions of the island's history, including the reigns of the Aragonese kings and the impact of the Black Death on Sicilian society. The work also reflects Bartholomew's own experiences as a jurist and his commitment to promoting the study of law and history. The Historia Sicula has been widely studied by historians and remains an important source for understanding the complex history of Sicily during this period.

This chronicle was commissioned by the King of Sicily, Frederick III, and reflects the patronage of the royal court in supporting the arts and humanities. Bartholomew's work demonstrates the importance of the Sicilian court in promoting cultural and intellectual achievements during this period. The Historia Sicula has been preserved in several manuscripts, including the famous manuscript of the Biblioteca Marciana in Venice, which dates back to the 14th century. This manuscript has been extensively studied by scholars, who have praised Bartholomew's work for its accuracy, detail, and insight into the history of Sicily.

The Historia Sicula has also been recognized for its contribution to the development of the chronicle genre in medieval Italy. Bartholomew's work demonstrates the importance of the chronicle in preserving historical records and promoting the study of history. The Historia Sicula has been widely praised by scholars for its accuracy, detail, and insight into the history of Sicily during the late Middle Ages.
